speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I understand you are a newborn presenting with feeding intolerance and bilious vomiting; this is a serious condition that requires us to determine the underlying cause quickly. To begin, has your vomiting been every time you feed, and do you notice any abdominal distension or blood in the stool?

speaker: Patient
text: Newborn, 3050-g (6-lb 12-oz) male, six hours post delivery. The newborn has had several episodes of bilious vomiting and is intolerant to feeding since birth. Was born at term following an uncomplicated pregnancy, though the mother missed several prenatal checkups. The patient's older brother underwent surgery for pyloric stenosis as an infant.

speaker: Doctor
text: The timing of the bilious vomiting starting within six hours of birth is a critical detail; this strongly suggests a distal obstruction like malrotation with volvulus rather than pyloric stenosis, which typically presents at 3-6 weeks of age. Did the mother notice any green-colored stool or blood mixed in the stool, and has the baby passed meconium yet?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Bilious vomiting. I also have Feeding intolerance, No fever, Vomiting started within first day after birth.
